Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I hereby request the following records:
Any and all records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of any investigation into Michael A. "Butch" Quarcini.
• Full Name: Michael A. "Butch" Quarcini
• DOB: February 7, 1931
• DOD: July 12, 2003
• Proof of Death: Attached is a link to Michael "Butch" Quarcini's obituary in the Buffalo News. Because the subject is deceased, personal privacy exemptions under Exemption 7(C) are severely diminished or no longer apply.
Background Summary for Context:
• Led LIUNA Local 91 in Niagara Falls, NY.
• Oversaw the Love Canal Cleanup Project for Local 91.
• Indicted by the federal government in May 2002 for racketeering and extortion via Local 91.
• Federal Informant Ronald Fino was told by Buffalo LCN member Leonard Falzone that Michael Quarcini answered to the Buffalo LCN Family and was a "good earner."
• Federal Informant Ronald Fino indicates Michael Quarcini was elected to his position in LIUNA Local 91 with the blessing of Stefano Magaddino's son-in-law James V. "Jimmy" LaDuca and Benjamin A. "Benny" Nicolletti Sr., who were both made men in the Buffalo LCN family.
• Federal Informant Ronald Fino indicates Michael Quarcini was close to Buffalo LCN member Danny Sansanese Jr.
Search Directions:
1. Field Office Records: Please conduct a thorough search for records at the FBI Field Office in Buffalo, NY, as well as FBI Headquarters (FBIHQ).
2. Cross-Reference and Associational Search: Be sure to search for references to Michael Quarcini in main files and cross-references related to the following individuals:
	• A. Leonard Falzone (DOD: November 12, 2016)
	• B. Stefano "Steve" Magaddino (DOD: July 19, 1974)
	• C. James "Jimmy" LaDuca (DOD: September 27, 1993)
	• D. Benjamin "Benny" Nicolletti Sr. (DOD: May 22, 1982)
	• E. Roy Carlisi (DOD: April 29, 1980)
	• F. Joseph Todaro Sr. (DOD: December 26, 2012)
	• G. Daniel Sansanese Jr. (DOD: April 16, 2003)
3. Indices Search: Conduct a search of the Central Records System (CRS) for Michael Quarcini, to explicitly include:
	• A. The Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices
	• B. The Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices
	• C. The Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices
	• D. The Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices
4. Scope of Search: In the above searches, please include both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies, and companies.
5. Archival Holdings: Please ensure this search covers retired, paper, or archived files, including searches of holdings transferred to or housed at the Alexandria Records Center or other offsite Bureau storage repositories.
6. Destroyed/Transferred Files: If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to the National Archives (NARA), I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips, as well as any other documentation describing said action.
7. Rolling Release: If previously processed or easily accessible records are available, I request a rolling, interim release consisting of those records while the remainder of the request is processed.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. § 552, I respectfully request access to records maintained by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a component of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), concerning U.S. entry restrictions, admissibility reviews, and interagency communications involving Mexican government officials, elected representatives, and political figures, including individuals affiliated with Mexico's National Regeneration Movement (Morena).

This request concerns official U.S. government actions and institutional coordination regarding restrictions affecting Mexican public officials.

I request records created or received between January 1, 2025, and November 2, 2026, including:

Existing administrative reports, statistical summaries, briefing documents, or internal assessments concerning restrictions on admission to the United States involving Mexican public officials, including governors, mayors, legislators, senior government officials, and political party leaders.

Official correspondence, memoranda, and interagency communications between CBP, the Department of State, and other DHS components concerning the implementation or coordination of entry restrictions affecting Mexican government officials.

Final policy guidance, administrative instructions, and memoranda concerning procedures used by CBP to implement visa-related restrictions, inadmissibility determinations, or entry limitations communicated by the Department of State or other federal agencies.

Existing aggregate statistical reports showing the number of Mexican nationals identified in official records as government officials or elected representatives who were subject to entry restrictions, inadmissibility determinations, or other relevant administrative measures, where such information is already compiled and can lawfully be disclosed.

Final internal briefing memoranda, official meeting summaries, and interagency coordination documents concerning restrictions affecting Mexican public officials in connection with corruption, organized crime, national security, or other statutory grounds of inadmissibility.

Records of official communications between CBP headquarters and U.S. government personnel assigned to Mexico concerning the implementation of entry restrictions affecting Mexican public officials.

Final or approved public affairs guidance, prepared questions and answers, and communications materials regarding public reporting about U.S. entry restrictions or visa cancellations involving Mexican political figures, including Morena-affiliated officials.

Please search, as appropriate, records maintained by:

CBP Office of Field Operations (OFO), including headquarters units responsible for admissibility and passenger programs.

CBP headquarters offices responsible for policy implementation and interagency coordination.

Other CBP offices reasonably likely to maintain responsive policy or administrative records.

Relevant search terms may include:

"Mexico," "Mexican government officials," "Mexican politicians," "Morena," "Mexican governors," "entry restrictions," "inadmissibility," "visa revocation," "visa cancellation," "admissibility review," "Department of State," "corruption," and "organized crime."

Scope and Privacy Limitations

This request does not seek individual immigration files, passport numbers, biometric records, personal travel histories, confidential visa applications, or sensitive law enforcement information.

I recognize that certain records may be protected under applicable privacy, immigration, national security, or law enforcement exemptions.

I am requesting existing institutional records concerning U.S. government policies, procedures, administrative decisions, statistical summaries, and interagency coordination.

Where responsive documents contain protected personal information, I request the release of all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.

This request does not require CBP to create a new list, statistical report, or analysis.

Fee Classification and Public Interest Waiver

I am a journalist conducting research for public-interest reporting concerning U.S.–Mexico relations, immigration policy, and government accountability.

I respectfully request classification under the news media fee category and a waiver of applicable fees because disclosure of the requested information would contribute to public understanding of the activities and decisions of the United States government.

The requested information is not intended primarily for commercial use.

Please provide responsive records electronically, preferably in searchable PDF format or their original electronic format where available.

If any records are withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemptions and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt information.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Hiroshi Takahashi

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

This request seeks existing government records and does not ask the Department to create a new list, prediction, or assessment.

Fee Classification and Waiver

I am a journalist conducting research for public-interest reporting about the diplomatic relationship between the United States and Mexico.

I respectfully request classification under the news media fee category and a waiver of applicable fees because disclosure would contribute to public understanding of U.S. government actions and policies.

Please provide responsive records electronically.

If any records are withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemptions and release all reasonably segregable information.

title: U.S. Diplomatic Communications Regarding ProPublica's January 2024 Investigation of Andrés Manuel López Obrador (Drug Enforcement Administration)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. § 552, I respectfully request copies of records held by the U.S. Department of State concerning the diplomatic response to the January 30, 2024, ProPublica investigation titled “Did Drug Traffickers Funnel Millions of Dollars to Mexican President López Obrador’s First Campaign?”, written by journalist Tim Golden.

The investigation described a previously undisclosed Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) inquiry into allegations of drug cartel contributions to Andrés Manuel López Obrador's 2006 presidential campaign.

Following publication, President López Obrador publicly accused U.S. government agencies of involvement in the disclosure, demanded an explanation and an apology from Washington, and questioned the implications for bilateral cooperation on migration, security, and counternarcotics.

I request records created or received between January 30 and September 30, 2024, including:

Internal correspondence, memoranda, and official communications between the Department of State, the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, and relevant diplomatic offices regarding the publication of the ProPublica investigation and the Mexican government's response.

Diplomatic cables, situation reports, briefing memoranda, and assessments concerning the potential impact of the controversy on U.S.–Mexico bilateral relations.

Official correspondence, meeting summaries, and records of communications between U.S. diplomatic officials and representatives of the Mexican government addressing the allegations, the reported DEA investigation, or the Mexican president's requests for clarification or an apology.

Final or approved press guidance, talking points, prepared questions and answers, and internal communications concerning the U.S. government's public response to the controversy.

Records documenting whether U.S. officials assessed possible consequences for bilateral cooperation involving migration, border security, intelligence sharing, or counternarcotics operations.

Final briefing materials and meeting readouts prepared for senior Department of State officials or the U.S. Ambassador to Mexico concerning the diplomatic implications of the controversy.

Please search records maintained by the following offices, to the extent they are likely to possess responsive documents:

Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs (WHA).

U.S. Embassy Mexico City, including its Political Section.

Bureau of Global Public Affairs and relevant press offices.

Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL).

Office of the Secretary of State, where responsive records may exist.

Relevant search terms may include:

"Andrés Manuel López Obrador," "AMLO," "ProPublica," "Tim Golden," "DEA investigation," "2006 campaign," "Operation Polanco," "Mexico diplomatic relations," and "apology."

This request concerns the diplomatic and institutional response of the United States government to a publicly reported controversy. It does not seek confidential informant identities, protected personal information, or underlying DEA investigative files.

Please provide all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of responsive records, including documents that may be partially redacted.

I request electronic delivery of the records.

Fee Classification and Public Interest Waiver

I am a journalist requesting these documents for news-gathering and public-interest reporting purposes.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: U.S. Embassy London Renunciation Appointment Demand and Waitlist Statistics (Whole 2024 – October 2026)
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request records maintained by the U.S. Department of State, including the Bureau of Consular Affairs and the American Citizen Services section of the U.S. Embassy in London, concerning demand for services relating to formal renunciation of U.S. nationality under INA § 349(a)(5), 8 U.S.C. § 1481(a)(5).

**Date range:** January 1, 2024, through October 31, 2026.

I request existing reports, spreadsheets, databases, dashboards, statistical summaries, appointment-management records, and routinely generated exports containing any of the following information:

1. **Initial requests:** The number of individuals newly requesting renunciation appointments or joining a renunciation appointment waitlist, preferably broken down by calendar month.

2. **Waitlist size:** The number of individuals awaiting renunciation appointments, including any existing monthly or periodic snapshots of the waiting list.

3. **Appointment offers and scheduling:** The number of renunciation appointments offered, scheduled, cancelled, or rescheduled, preferably broken down by calendar month.

4. **Completed appointments:** The number of completed in-person renunciation appointments or oaths of renunciation, preferably broken down by calendar month.

5. **Waiting times:** Existing reports or summaries showing the time between an individual's initial appointment request or waitlist registration and the date an appointment was offered or held.

6. **Appointment capacity:** Existing statistical reports showing the number of renunciation appointment slots allocated or made available during the requested period.

The purpose of this request is to examine changes in demand and appointment processing before and after April 13, 2026, when the administrative processing fee for a Certificate of Loss of Nationality decreased from $2,350 to $450.

**Scope and format**

I seek existing records, not newly prepared statistical analyses. Where monthly aggregates are unavailable, please provide the closest available periodic reports or existing electronic tabular records containing the requested information.

I do not seek individuals' names, contact information, identification numbers, individual case files, or the contents of individual correspondence. If records contain personally identifiable information, please release reasonably segregable aggregate data or non-identifying fields.

Where available, please distinguish formal renunciations under INA § 349(a)(5) from other relinquishment requests under INA § 349(a)(1)–(4).

Please provide responsive records electronically, preferably in their native formats, including CSV or XLSX for tabular records.

If some requested categories are not maintained, please process the remaining categories independently rather than treating the request as indivisible. If clarification or narrowing would materially facilitate processing, please contact me before making an adverse determination.

**Fees and public interest**

This request is noncommercial. The information concerns public access to a federal consular service and the effects of a substantial change in government fees. I intend to make responsive records publicly available through MuckRock.

I request a waiver of applicable processing fees on public-interest grounds. If a waiver is denied, I agree to pay up to $25 in applicable fees and request advance notification before incurring any greater amount.

Please acknowledge receipt, assign a tracking number, and provide any records available for release on a rolling basis.

Thank you for your consideration,
Nicholas Lee

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Worldwide Renunciation Demand, CLN Applications, and Processing Statistics, Whole 2024 – October 2026
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request records maintained by the U.S. Department of State, particularly the Bureau of Consular Affairs, Office of American Citizen Services (CA/OCS/ACS), concerning the volume of requests for Certificates of Loss of Nationality (CLNs) and associated renunciation services.

**Date range:** January 1, 2024, through October 31, 2026.

I request existing statistical reports, spreadsheets, dashboards, database exports, management summaries, or other aggregate records reflecting:

1. The number of new requests for renunciation or CLN services received by U.S. diplomatic and consular posts, where centrally compiled statistics exist.

2. The number of CLN application packages received by CA/OCS/ACS from overseas posts.

3. The number of CLNs approved and denied by the Department of State.

4. The number of CLN applications pending review or adjudication, where periodic backlog statistics are maintained.

5. Any existing statistical breakdown of these figures by month or quarter and by diplomatic or consular post.

Where the records distinguish formal renunciation under INA § 349(a)(5) from other relinquishment cases under INA § 349(a)(1)–(4), please preserve this distinction.

This request is intended to facilitate comparison of application demand and processing volumes before and after the reduction of the CLN administrative processing fee from $2,350 to $450, effective April 13, 2026.

**Relevant prior disclosure**

The Department previously released fiscal-year CLN approval statistics in response to FOIA request F-2025-01674, submitted by Malakouti Law and answered April 10, 2025.

I request the corresponding existing records for the more recent period, together with any available monthly, quarterly, post-level, or case-intake statistics.

**Scope and format**

This request seeks existing records and reasonably retrievable electronic data, not the preparation of a new statistical study.

For worldwide figures, please prioritize records already maintained centrally by CA/OCS/ACS rather than requiring searches of individual case files or correspondence at every overseas post.

No personally identifiable information is requested. Please release reasonably segregable non-identifying statistical information.

Please provide responsive records electronically, with tabular information in its native CSV, XLSX, or equivalent format where available.

If certain categories are unavailable or would require substantially disproportionate search efforts, please process the remaining categories independently and contact me to discuss narrowing the scope.

**Fees and public interest**

This request is noncommercial and intended to inform public discussion of citizenship renunciation, access to consular services, and changes in demand following the 2026 fee reduction.

I intend to make responsive records publicly accessible through MuckRock and request a public-interest fee waiver.

If the waiver is denied, I agree to pay up to $25 in fees, with advance notification required for any greater amount.

Please acknowledge receipt, provide a tracking number, and release responsive records on a rolling basis where feasible.

Thank you for your consideration,
Nicholas Lee

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Prior FOIA requests establish that the Chief Immigration Judge has provided unlawful instructions to Immigration Judges regarding how to rule on certain motions. Given the due process right to a neutral arbiter, I am filing this request.

To that end, please produce the e-mail, Teams, Slack, and Signal messages from January 20, 2025, to the present that mention any of the following keywords:

"Matter of C-A-R-R-*" or "In re C-A-R-R-*"

Please note that I am using the asterisk (*) to designate the standard use of “wildcards” in the search for responsive records. For example, a search for “pretermi*” would return all of the following: pretermission, pretermit, pretermitted, etc. If you are unable to search for wildcards, please advise so that I may specifically include the variations I would like searched.

The search should include the following Immigration Judges' e-mail, Teams, Slack and Signal accounts:
Sirce Owen
Teresa Riley
Keith E. Hunsucker

2. In addition to the records requested above, I also request records describing the processing of this request, including records sufficient to identify search terms used and locations and custodians searched and any tracking sheets used to track the processing of this request. If you use FOIA questionnaires or certifications completed by individual custodians or components to determine whether they possess responsive materials or to describe how they conducted searches, I also request any such records prepared in connection with the processing of this request.

Please note it is unlawful to assign the task of e-mail searches to the e-mail custodians themselves.

Please search all records regarding agency business. You may not exclude searches of files or emails in the personal custody of your officials, such as personal email accounts or personal Skype accounts. Records of official business conducted using unofficial systems or stored outside of official files are subject to the Federal Records Act and FOIA. See Competitive Enter. Inst. v. Office of Sci. & Tech. Policy,  241 F. Supp. 3d 14, 24 (D.D.C. 2017).

It is not adequate to rely on policies and procedures that require officials to move such information to official systems within a certain period of time; I exercise and specifically preserve and assert my right to records contained in those files even if material has not yet been moved to official systems or if officials have, through negligence or willfulness, failed to meet their obligations. 

In addition, please note that in conducting a “reasonable search” as required by law, you must employ the most up-to-date technologies and tools available, in addition to searches by individual custodians likely to have responsive information. 

Furthermore, agencies that have adopted the National Archives and Records Agency (NARA) Capstone program, or similar policies, now maintain emails in a form that is reasonably likely to be more complete than individual custodians’ files. For example, a custodian may have deleted a responsive email from his or her email program, but DOJ’s archiving tools would capture that email under Capstone. Accordingly, I insist that the EOIR use the most up-to-date technologies to search for responsive information and take steps to ensure that the most complete repositories of information are searched. I am available to work with you to craft appropriate search terms.

If it is your position that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, I request that you provide an index of those documents as required under Vaughn v. Rosen, 484 F.2d 820 (D.C. Cir. 1973), cert. denied, 415 U.S. 977 (1974). The index must describe each document claimed as exempt with sufficient specificity “to permit a reasoned judgment as to whether the material is actually exempt under FOIA.” Founding Church of Scientology v. Bell, 603 F.2d 945, 949 (D.C. Cir. 1979). Moreover, the index “must describe each document or portion thereof withheld, and for each withholding it must discuss the consequences of disclosing the sought-after information.” King v. U.S. Dep’t of Justice, 830 F.2d 210, 223–24 (D.C. Cir. 1987). Further, “the withholding agency must supply ‘a relatively detailed justification, specifically identifying the reasons why a particular exemption is relevant and correlating those claims with the particular part of a withheld document to which they apply.’” Id. at 224 (citing Mead Data Central, Inc. v. U.S. Dep’t of the Air Force, 566 F.2d 242, 251 (D.C. Cir. 1977)).

In the event some portions of the requested records are properly exempt from disclosure, please disclose any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of the requested records. If it is your position that a record contains non-exempt segments, but that those non-exempt segments are so dispersed throughout the document as to make segregation impossible, please state what portion of the document is non-exempt, and how the material is dispersed throughout the document. Mead Data Central, 566 F.2d at 261. Claims of nonsegregability must be made with the same degree of detail as required for claims of exemptions in a Vaughn index. If a request is denied in whole, please state specifically that it is not reasonable to segregate portions of the record for release.

Expedite Request:
Pursuant to 6 CFR § 5.5(e)(1) I am requesting the processing and production of records in response to this request be expedited. In particular, to the extent that the Chief Immigration Judge is ordering Judges to grant motions to pretermit and therefore precluding immigrants from the right to a neutral arbiter, the matter is especially urgent. As outlined above, I am primarily engaged in disseminating information. The loss of substantial due process rights cannot be overstated. communications.communication:
Dear Lara Nochomovitz, 

This response acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request by the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR).  Your request has been assigned control number 2027-05527. 

Please be advised that the status of requests submitted through the Public Access Link (PAL) may be tracked at https://foia.eoir.justice.gov/app/Home.aspx, and you will receive an email response to your request upon completion of processing. The status of requests submitted by email or mail may not be trackable through the PAL, but you will still receive an email or mailed response to your request upon completion of processing. (https://foia.eoir.justice.gov/app/Home.aspx) Please ensure the email address you provided in PAL will be able to receive the messages we send you. Messages rejected by your email account will not be rerouted to you. 
Please be aware that EOIR is a component of the Department of Justice and the custodian of records for the “Record of Proceedings” (ROP), which is the compilation of documents and digital audio recordings produced in proceedings before the immigration courts and the BIA. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is the custodian of records for the “A-file,” which is a series of records of a person’s immigration history and is maintained and stored by DHS. EOIR is not the custodian of records for DHS or its components, nor does EOIR have access to DHS’s A-files. EOIR does not create an ROP until matters are initiated by DHS. Nevertheless, EOIR may create and maintain ROPs for proceedings other than removal proceedings (i.e., credible fear reviews, bond hearings). You may request a copy of your Notice to Appear (NTA) and full A-file from DHS. (https://www.dhs.gov/foia) 
Note that parties to immigration cases (including respondents and their representatives of record) have the option to request their Record of Proceedings directly from the immigration court or Board of Immigration Appeals. Please see the instructions here: https://www.justice.gov/eoir/ROPrequest. (https://www.justice.gov/eoir/ROPrequest) 

If you have filed a fee waiver request, EOIR will address the fee waiver in a separate letter. Most requests for records of proceedings do not require any fees; however, if the fees for processing the request are estimated to exceed $25.00, EOIR will notify you before processing the request to determine whether you will commit to paying the fee or whether you wish to narrow the scope of your request to reduce the fee. Fees may be charged for searching records at the rate of $4.75 (administrative)/$10.00 (professional) per quarter hour, and for duplication of copies at the rate of $.05 per copy. The first 100 copies and two hours of search time are not charged, and charges must exceed $25.00 before we will charge a fee. 

The FOIA requires an agency to respond within 20 working days after receipt of the request, and EOIR endeavors to meet this standard.  The FOIA permits a ten-day extension of this time period, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B), based on unusual circumstances.  Your request involves “unusual circumstances,” and EOIR is extending the time period to respond by an additional 10 working days because your request requires the collection of records from field offices, or involves a search, collection, and review of voluminous records, or requires consultation with another agency or two or more agency components. 

EOIR FOIA requests are placed in one of three tracks. Track one is for those requests that seek and receive expedited processing pursuant to subsection (a)(6)(E) of the FOIA. Track two is for simple requests that do not involve voluminous records or lengthy consultations with other entities.  Track three is for complex requests that involve voluminous records and for which lengthy or numerous consultations are required, or those requests that may involve sensitive records.  As a matter of default, your request has been placed in track two for simple requests.  If you have requested expedited processing, EOIR will contact you in a separate letter. 

If you have any questions regarding unusual circumstances, you may contact the EOIR FOIA Service Center or FOIA Public Liaison at EOIR.FOIArequests@usdoj.gov to discuss reformulation or an alternative time frame to process your request, or for any further assistance regarding any aspect of your request. Alternatively, you may contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at the National Archives and Records Administration to inquire about the FOIA mediation services they offer.  The contact information for OGIS is as follows: Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, Room 2510, 8601 Adelphi Road, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001; e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at (202) 741-5770; toll free at (877) 684-6448; or facsimile at (202) 741-5769. 
 
Sincerely, 

FOIA Intake
